Customers found it difficult to avail quality services in a convenient manner, and service professionals were struggling to make ends meet, having to rely upon several middlemen, contractors, and local aggregators. The founders felt that the industry was ripe for disruption, and launched Urban Company, with three key principles in mind:

 ● Partner empowerment: Build a deep, full\-stack partnership with service partners, helping improve their earnings and overall livelihood
 



 ● Technology first: Bring innovation and technology to an age\-old industry.

 **AI graphic des** 
 igner who lives at the intersection of design, social media and generative tools. This is not a ‘take brief, wait for feedback, make rounds’ role.  At UC, you’ll get to work on category\-defining narratives that influence not just our business but the broader culture of work, care, and dignity. description:
**Company Description** 




  





 Spur (https://spur.so) is an agentic CRM for businesses that sell to consumers over chat. 600\+ businesses across 50\+ countries run on Spur, around 5 million conversations a month: ecommerce brands first, and increasingly anyone whose customers message them on WhatsApp and Instagram, from real estate and travel to education, clinics and services. Every WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, email and live chat message lands in one inbox with AI handling most of it, and the same platform runs their campaigns, lead follow\-up, abandoned cart recovery and website conversion.
 



  





 We're bootstrapped and profitable. Zero external funding, zero marketing spend. We're 12 people: 2 founders, 3 engineers, 5 in customer success, 1 founding marketer, 1 AE.
 



  





**Role Description** 




  





 Three engineers, two founders, 600\+ brands running their entire customer conversation on what we've built, and nobody whose job is how it works. That's what we're fixing.
 



  





 You'll build our design system and then make it stick, which is the harder half: the components, the patterns, the rules, and the conversations with engineers about why a rule exists. A system nobody follows is a Figma file, not a system.
 



  





 The rest of the job is design decisions, end to end, and at Spur that means more than screens. When Meta ships something new on WhatsApp, you're the person who reads the documentation, talks to the engineers about what it costs to build, talks to merchants about whether they'd use it, and comes back with what we should build and how it should work. You'll sit with customer success, who hear every complaint, and with the AE, who hears every objection, and neither of them will have to chase you for it.
 



  





**You'll probably be a fit if you** 




  




* Have built a design system that other people actually used, and can tell us how you got them to use it
* Talk to customers yourself instead of receiving their opinions secondhand
* Read platform and API documentation without being thrown by it
* Have shipped in a small team with no PM layer and no handoff ceremony
* Use AI daily and have built something with it, even a no\-code automation, to kill a repetitive task



  





**Bonus points** 




  




* You've designed for messaging, commerce, or anything with a real\-time inbox in it
* You've worked on a Shopify app, or with Shopify merchants
* You write front end code well enough to prototype, or to argue with an engineer in their own terms
* You know the WhatsApp Business API or Meta's business tools from the inside



  





**Logistics** 




  




* Five days a week in our Green Park, Delhi office
* You'll be the first designer here, working directly with both founders and all three engineers
* Appraisals every 12 months. Our motto: if Spur grows, the team should be the first to benefit



  





 We read every response ourselves, and you'll hear back either way.

title: CRO Lead
description:
**OneMetric \| Full\-time \| Gurgaon**
****The role in one line****
 This is not a "manage the website" role or a CRO role for its own sake — it's a lead\-generation role that uses the website as the primary lever. You own the website end to end — from a raw idea for a page to a shipped, converting landing page — against one defined outcome: 35–50 MQLs a month generated organically from the website and the motions around it.
   

  

****Why this role exists****
 Most people who "manage the website" either write copy and hand it to a designer, or build pages and wait for someone else to tell them what to put on them. We need someone who does both halves in one head: knows what a page needs to say because they've done the research and talked to customers, and knows why a page converts or doesn't because they think like a CRO person, not just a writer or a builder. The output is a live, working page — not a doc that someone else has to translate.
   

  

******What You'll Own******
* The website as a whole — structure, page inventory, and how it evolves as the company's positioning evolves.
* Idea → live page. You take a rough brief ("we need a page for X service" or "we're repositioning around Y") and turn it into a wireframe, then real copy, then a shipped page — working with a designer where needed, but driving the thing yourself.
* Conversion performance — what's converting, what isn't, and why. You run the experiments, not just report the numbers.
* Lead capture and funnel logic on\-site — forms, CTAs, gating, the path from a visitor landing on a page to becoming a lead in HubSpot.
* The lead number. 35–50 organic leads/month from the website and the motions around it (SEO, AEO, on\-site conversion, content) is your number. The page isn't done when it ships — it's done when it's producing.


****What you'll actually do, week to week****
* Talk to customers and internal stakeholders (sales, delivery, leadership) to figure out what a page actually needs to say to move a buyer — not guess at it from a template.
* Look at signals — search intent, competitor positioning, what prospects ask sales, what's converting elsewhere — and turn them into a point of view on what the page should be.
* Write the copy yourself. This isn't a hand\-off role — strong, clear, buyer\-facing writing is a core skill here, not a nice\-to\-have.
* Sketch wireframes and work directly with a designer (or design tools yourself) to get from idea to a real, live example fast.
* Build and manage pages in WordPress and HubSpot CMS.
* Use AI tools (Claude and others) and Figma as part of your everyday workflow — for research, drafting, quick mockups, and design iteration.
* Structure pages and content for both traditional SEO and AEO (answer engine optimization) — so the site shows up in Google and gets cited by AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and AI Overviews.
* Track what's converting and what's not, and keep iterating rather than treating a page as "done" once it ships.


****What we need****
* A CRO brain. You should be able to look at a page and say, with reasons, why it will or won't convert — and know how to fix it. This means understanding funnels, lead capture mechanics, and what actually moves a B2B buyer to act.
* Strong writing, in service of strategy. You can write clean, persuasive copy, but more importantly you know what needs to be said and why, before you write a word.
* A founder/CMO\-level eye for B2B design. You don't need to be the designer, but you need the taste to know what good B2B design looks like and the ability to brief and push back on one.
* The ability to simplify. You can take a genuinely complex service or technical concept (a RevOps build, an AI GTM agent) and explain it in language a buyer actually understands.
* A working understanding of AEO and SEO. You know how to structure and write content so it ranks in search and gets picked up and cited by AI answer engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) — this isn't optional anymore for a website role.
* Strong writing skills paired with AI fluency. You write well yourself, and you use AI tools to move fast — generating quick mockups, drafts, and iterations rather than waiting on a full design cycle for every idea.
* Comfort with the tools: WordPress, HubSpot CMS, Figma, and AI tools (Claude and similar) as part of daily work.
* Ownership instinct — you treat the website as yours, not as a queue of tickets from other teams.
* 4–5 years of experience working on websites/landing pages, ideally with direct exposure to conversion work, not just content or design in isolation.


****What's in it for you****
* Ownership, not a task list. We don't hand you a checklist and check boxes. Direction and context get discussed openly, and then the "how" — the wireframe, the copy, the page — is yours to run with.
* A performance\-driven culture. Speed and conversion results define your trajectory here, not tenure or face\-time. Ship fast, see what moves the numbers, and get rewarded for it.
* Access to the top of the market. The pages you build speak to CMOs, VPs of Sales, and founders across the B2B US market — real high\-stakes work, not busywork nobody reads.


****How we'll know this is working****
 Within a quarter: organic leads from the website and its motions are trending toward the 35–50/month range, pages you've shipped are outperforming what existed before on conversion, sales and leadership are coming to you first when a new page or repositioning is needed, and the website stops feeling like a static asset and starts feeling like something that's actively working for the business.
   

  

******Who You'll Work With******
 Reports into growth/marketing leadership at OneMetric, works closely with sales, delivery leads, and a designer (in\-house or external) to take ideas from brief to live page.
   

  

******Who You'll Work With******
 This role reports to the CEO’s office at OneMetric and works closely with sales and delivery leaders on HubSpot implementation, RevOps, and GTM projects.

title: Marketing Designer
description:
Portcast is a venture\-backed, Singapore\-based logistics technology company building AI\-powered intelligence for the freight forwarding industry. Freight forwarders manage thousands of shipments, rates, exceptions, and operational decisions every day. The challenge is not a lack of data. It is knowing what needs attention, what is going wrong, and what action to take next.
   

  

 Portcast uses AI and data to help freight forwarders surface shipment exceptions, identify cost and margin risks, and make better decisions across the shipment lifecycle. Our products help teams improve operational efficiency, protect margins, and make faster, more informed decisions. Our vision is to become the AI data and intelligence layer that powers exception management and margin improvement on every shipment.
   

  

 Founded in 2018 and backed by leading technology investors, we are a lean, globally distributed team building technology for an industry going through a major digital transformation.
   

  

**ABOUT THE ROLE:**
 We are looking for a Marketing Designer to be the design engine behind our marketing. You'll turn briefs and copy into polished, on\-brand assets across the full funnel, landing pages, case studies, social and paid creative, event materials, product collateral, and video, often at speed and across several formats at once. You'll partner closely with content and growth marketing (copy and content sit with the Content Marketing Manager; the visual craft is yours) to keep a consistent visual system across everything we publish, and raise the bar on how the Portcast brand shows up.
   

  

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:**
* A consistent, high\-quality visual system across everything Portcast publishes, with assets shipped quickly and on\-brand across web, print, social, paid, and video, so marketing can move fast without design becoming a bottleneck or losing craft.


**WHAT YOU’LL OWN:**
* Design landing pages, case study PDFs, product one\-pagers, and sales/product collateral
* Produce social creative (LinkedIn\-first), including post series and campaign templates
* Build paid media and creative for LinkedIn and Google campaigns across personas
* Create event and webinar assets: banners, booth graphics, decks
* Produce and edit video content end to end, short\-form social clips, product feature videos, webinar/event recaps, and launch teasers, from raw footage to polished, on\-brand output
* Maintain and extend the Portcast brand system: components, tokens, templates
* Support HTML email/newsletter production and light web design handoff
* Iterate quickly across multiple design and content review rounds


**WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:**
* Bachelor's or Master's in Marketing, Business, or a related field, or equivalent
* At least 3\+ years in a design role, ideally in\-house at a B2B SaaS product\-based startup or at an agency doing B2B marketing, with a portfolio that shows real range across web, print, social, campaign, and video work
* Fast, high\-craft execution: You produce polished work quickly, often across several formats at once, without letting speed erode quality. You take direction and iterate well, but you hold your own opinions on what "good" looks like
* Detail\-obsessed: Pixel alignment, spacing, and consistency matter to you. You catch the small things others miss and hold the visual bar across everything that ships
* Figma (advanced): You work fluently with components, variants, auto\-layout, and shared libraries, and you keep the design system clean and reusable
* Adobe Creative Suite: Strong in Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign, including multi\-page, print\-ready layouts for case studies and collateral
* Design fundamentals: A strong grasp of typography, layout, grid systems, and brand consistency, and the ability to design for web and print formats interchangeably
* Creative at scale: You're comfortable designing social and paid ad creative at volume from templates, keeping everything on\-brand across personas and campaigns
* Video editing and production: You can take a project from raw footage to finished, high\-quality output, cutting, pacing, color, captions/subtitles, motion titles, and sound. You're fluent in Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects (or equivalent DaVinci Resolve / Final Cut), and CapCut or similar for fast short\-form social edits
* Web and email handoff: A basic understanding of HTML/CSS, enough to work within existing markup for email and web handoff, not necessarily coding from scratch
* Brand systems: Working knowledge of brand systems and design tokens, and how to keep every asset on\-system as the brand scales
* Advanced motion design: animation and motion work (Lottie, complex After Effects, 3D/Blender)
* Presentation design: high\-polish decks in PowerPoint or Google Slides
* AI design tooling: familiarity with image generation, AI\-assisted layout, prompt\-based workflows, and AI video
* Webflow basics: building or maintaining pages in Webflow, not just designing them
* Curiosity for the logistics domain: Experiencein logistics, supply chain, transportation, or freight technology is valued, but so is a genuine curiosity to understand our market in depth
* AI\-forward mindset: You consistently apply AI across design workflows and actively experiment with new tools as they emerge
* Startup builder mentality: You thrive in lean, fast\-moving environments where ownership is high and resources are limited
* Strong communicator: You communicate clearly across a diverse, distributed, cross\-cultural team. You can be opinionated, but you engage with other views and compromise when it's right


**WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU:**
* Own the visual craft end to end: You'll own how Portcast looks and feels across everything we publish, with real influence over the brand and few layers between an idea and what ships.
* Build in an industry still defining modern B2B marketing: Logistics and supply chain tech is at an exciting stage of digital transformation, with significant room to rethink how enterprise software is marketed and how it looks. You'll bring fresh ideas, challenge conventional thinking, and help shape what great design looks like in this space.
* Work at the intersection of AI, design, and logistics: We have a strong product, established enterprise customers, and a real opportunity to sharpen how we show up. You'll get to push AI\-forward design and video workflows, not just execute templates.
* Small by design, fully distributed across Asia and Europe, built on trust, accountability, and collaboration. Your work directly shapes launches, customer perception, and how the market sees Portcast.


**OUR CORE VALUES GUIDE EVERYTHING WE DO:**
* Curiosity: We dig into why a design worked or didn't, how a freight forwarder actually operates, and what makes our brand land with customers.
* Ownership: We act like founders. We don't wait to be told what to make, and we stay on a piece until it's genuinely on\-brand and right.
* Raising the bar: We don't settle for assets that are merely fine. We hold a high standard for craft, polish, and the experience our brand creates.
* Effectiveness: We focus on design that drives real marketing outcomes, pipeline, launches, and brand perception, not just output. We prioritize the right work and make practical trade\-offs.


 Join us at Portcast and help shape the future of the logistics and shipping industry through design that is as sharp as the product behind it.

 We are building India's first agentic accounting harness — the runtime that lets an AI agent actually keep a company's books: read the ledger, write and run its own code in a sandbox, and check every result against the trial balance before it posts.
 



  





**You would be our first design hire.** 
 Not one of a team — the person who decides what design means here, and who grows into leading the function and building the team.
 



  





**WHERE WE ARE, IN NUMBERS** 



* **Already generating revenue** 
 from products and services live in market today.
* **Targeting ₹20 crore ARR inside twelve months** 
 — on our own revenue, from tools and services already launched, before we raise next.
* **Phase one ships December 2026\. Phase two ships March 2027\.** 
 An enterprise\-grade agentic ERP build lands by the end of December.



  





**THE MARKET** 



* Global ERP software is a
 **$106 billion market in 2026** 
 , forecast to reach
 **$281 billion by 2034** 
 . SMEs are already more than half of it — and the fastest\-growing half.
* There are roughly
 **400 million small and medium businesses on earth** 
 — 90% of all companies, 70% of all employment, and half of global GDP. Almost none of them can afford software that genuinely works.
* **Rillet** 
 is building roughly our thesis for the US alone. In August 2026 they raised
 **$100 million at a $1 billion valuation** 
 , two years out of stealth, on
 **$200M\+ total** 
 from ICONIQ, Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia. 600\+ customers, and
 **ARR doubled in three months** 
 . They are going straight at NetSuite.
* The incumbents — NetSuite, SAP, Sage, QuickBooks, Tally — were architected between the 1980s and the 1990s and priced for companies that could afford consultants to install them.
* **We are building this for the world.** 
 India is where we start, not where we stop: 7\.83 crore registered businesses, 1\.67 crore GST filers, and an incumbent turning over roughly $60 million on thirty\-year\-old software.
 **If an agentic ERP works at Indian price points and Indian compliance complexity, it works anywhere.**



**﻿**




**WHAT YOU WILL OWN** 



* Every module we have and every one we build next. New products from nothing, and existing ones that need to get better.
* The information architecture and navigation for our accounting suite — decided, defended, and stable.
* A component library our engineers build against without asking you questions.
* Voucher entry an accountant can drive from the keyboard at forty entries an hour without reaching for the mouse.
* The design language for everything that follows — payroll, expenses, reconciliation, the agentic layer.



  





**WHAT WE REQUIRE — please read before applying** 



* **3\+ years** 
 of full\-time product design experience after graduation. Internships and freelance do not count.
* **At least one design of yours is in production right now, used by thousands of people on a recurring basis.** 
 You must be able to name it, link it, and say roughly how many people use it. This is what we screen hardest on.
* **You code your own prototypes** 
 — React or Next.js, running in a browser. With or without AI assistance; we judge the output, not the method. A Figma file is not a prototype.
* Product design, not visual design. Flows, states, edge cases, empty screens, error handling — not brand systems or marketing pages.
* Data\-dense interface experience: dashboards, admin consoles, ERP or POS software, operations tools, complex forms and tables.



  





**STARTUP EXPERIENCE IS A REQUIREMENT, NOT A PREFERENCE** 




 We want people who have built inside a startup — ideally one
 **less than 4–5 years old** 
 when you were there. Being among the first 10–20 employees somewhere is the strongest signal we look for. If your entire career has been at large organisations with briefs handed to you, this will be an uncomfortable fit for both of us.
 



  





**WE ARE NOT FILTERING ON YOUR DEGREE.** 
 Design school, engineering college, or neither. What is in production and who uses it is the entire filter.
 



  





**THE HONEST PART** 



* **Compensation: ₹12–18 LPA fixed.**
* **Working days: six days a week, Monday to Saturday.** 
 We will move to five as soon as we are in a position to, and that is a commitment. But today it is six, and you should decide with that in front of you rather than find it out in month two.
* On\-site in New Delhi. Not remote, not hybrid.
* Relocating? We book and pay for your flight or train.



  





**WHAT YOU GET INSTEAD** 




 No bureaucracy — no approval chains, no committees. Full transparency on revenue, burn and runway; everyone here knows all three. And the chance to be the person who decided what this product looks like.
 



  





**DO NOT APPLY IF** 



* Your portfolio is concept work, unshipped case studies, or redesigns of famous apps.
* Nothing you have designed is currently used by strangers.
* You design in Figma and hand off.
* You are a brand, marketing or graphic designer moving into product.
* You want remote or hybrid, or a six\-day week does not work for you.

**Overview**

 You will set the organisation’s standard for problem framing, customer insight, interaction and visual craft, systems thinking, technical fluency, storytelling, and measurable design impact. **What you will own** 



* Long\-range experience direction for major product portfolios or company\-level initiatives.

* Raise the design bar for the most important initiatives and the development of senior design leadership.
* Opportunities for design to create new customer value, differentiation, growth, trust, or operating leverage.



  





**What you will do** 




**Shape company\-level product and experience strategy** 



* Set the gold standard for defining complex customer and business problems with clarity, depth, and strategic relevance.
* Identify opportunities that cut across existing organisational or product boundaries and build compelling cases for action.
* Define or co\-create long\-range experience visions that connect immediate delivery with Airtel’s future product and business direction.
* Balance foundational systems, near\-term outcomes, regulatory or operational realities, and bold future bets.
* Improve the organisation’s approach to customer research, experimentation, measurement, and post\-launch learning where current evidence is insufficient.



**Define the organisation’s design and systems bar** 



* Set and evolve standards for interaction design, visual design, information architecture, content, accessibility, prototyping, service experience, and implementation quality.
* Create principles, frameworks, and reusable behavioural patterns that allow teams to solve complex problems consistently without losing customer context.
* Identify systemic issues across journeys, platforms, channels, terminology, information architecture, and operational processes; lead programmes to resolve them.
* Connect and simplify complex systems while making the consequences of exceptions and trade\-offs explicit.
* Guide the evolution and governance of Airtel’s design system when current components or patterns are insufficient for the next generation of products.
* Shape responsible AI\-enabled products and design practices, including intent definition, behavioural rules, guardrails, feedback loops, explainability, failure recovery, and human oversight.
* Establish or sponsor organisation\-level quality mechanisms that protect the intended experience through build and release.



**Lead the organisation through influence** 



* Influence at every level through exceptional product judgment, evidence, design craft, and business understanding.
* Use prototypes and storytelling to make future opportunities tangible and enable strategic decisions.
* De\-escalate difficult situations, align senior leaders, and move initiatives through complex organisational constraints.
* Direct and critique the work of Lead and Senior Product Designers on the highest\-impact programmes.

**Increase the leverage of Design** 



* Identify where Design can unlock growth, reduce service effort, improve trust, increase adoption, or create new business models.

* Represent Airtel Design externally through writing, speaking, industry collaboration, or thought leadership when it creates value.
* Attract and develop exceptional design talent by setting a standard people want to learn from.



  





**What you will bring** 



* Typically 10\+ years of experience in Product Design, with substantial experience shaping complex products, platforms, or ecosystems at scale.
* A body of work demonstrating company\-level problem framing, long\-range vision, systems design, exceptional craft, and measurable business and customer impact.
* Deep expertise across product strategy, interaction design, visual design, information architecture, prototyping, and design systems.
* Strong fluency in research, data, technology, operations, and organisational decision\-making.
* The ability to reason across customer journeys, backend systems, assisted channels, policy, regulation, and service operations.
* A record of influencing executives and aligning multiple teams or business units around a coherent direction.
* A record of creating reusable frameworks or systems that improve outcomes beyond your own projects.
* Evidence of developing senior designers and raising organisational design quality through influence rather than hierarchy.
* Exceptional storytelling, facilitation, negotiation, conflict\-resolution, and written communication skills.



  





**Good to have** 



* Experience in fintech, telecom, banking, payments, identity, AI, marketplaces, platform ecosystems, or other regulated and high\-scale environments.
* Experience shaping products across consumer, enterprise, assisted, retail, and operational channels.
* Industry\-recognised work, public writing, speaking, patents, frameworks, or other external contribution.
* Experience defining new design\-system, AI interaction, or service\-experience conventions.



  





**What success looks like** 



* Airtel makes better portfolio and investment decisions because of your framing and influence.
* Major product areas converge around a coherent customer and experience direction.
* Systemic complexity is reduced rather than redistributed between teams or channels.
* The organisation ships products that are simpler for customers, scalable for technology, viable for the business, and workable for operations.
* Senior designers become stronger strategic and organisational leaders through your coaching.
* Airtel’s design standards, frameworks, and product experiences are recognised internally—and increasingly externally—as benchmarks for quality.
* Design creates measurable new value beyond interface delivery.
